tools_helpful.evidence: Turn ~5 bootstrap did the bulk Windows.UI.Xaml -> Microsoft.UI.Xaml rewrite and scaffolded the project; no complaints in the log.
Agent pulled -Anchor manifest / manifest-migration-checklist / csproj / windowing patterns and applied them cleanly.
Run near the end to gate the migration; final build succeeded and app launched.

tool_limitations.limitation: When the build fails with CS0234 into the project's OWN namespace (project name equals a WinRT type name), the validator prints the generic 'Common build errors after the namespace rewrite' hint, which does not surface the true root cause (name collision).
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add a targeted diagnostic: when a CS0234 error's namespace token equals the project base name, point the agent at the namespace-collision pattern.

failed_apis.why_tried: Sample calls KeyCredentialManager.OpenAsync(...) unqualified, as in the original UWP source.
failed_apis.root_cause: The WinUI project (and thus root namespace) is named 'KeyCredentialManager', identical to the WinRT class. Unqualified 'KeyCredentialManager.OpenAsync' binds to the project namespace, so the member (OpenAsync) is not found -> CS0234.
failed_apis.fix: Add a using-alias 'using KeyCredentialManagerWinRT = Windows.Security.Credentials.KeyCredentialManager;' and rewrite the calls to the alias (or fully qualify / use global::).

special_apis.special_handling: Windows-universal-samples are commonly named after the API they demo; keeping the project name equal to the WinRT type shadows it. Alias or fully-qualify the WinRT class.

errors_encountered.error: CS0234: The type or namespace name 'OpenAsync' does not exist in the namespace 'KeyCredentialManager' (x5, also DeleteAsync/IsSupportedAsync/RequestCreateAsync)
errors_encountered.root_cause: Project/root namespace name collides with the WinRT class name; unqualified static calls resolve to the app namespace.
errors_encountered.fix: using-alias to Windows.Security.Credentials.KeyCredentialManager, then call via the alias.

errors_encountered.error: XamlCompiler warning WMC1509 + Xaml Internal Error WMC9999: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
errors_encountered.root_cause: Cascade of the C# CS0234 failures: because the C# compile failed, MarkupCompilePass2 had no LocalAssembly and the markup compiler crashed. NOT an independent XAML bug.
errors_encountered.fix: Resolving the CS0234 namespace collision made the WMC1509/WMC9999 disappear on the next build.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Build failed with 6 errors / repeated CS0234 into namespace 'KeyCredentialManager' plus a scary WMC9999 XAML internal error.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: ~10 turns (diagnose collision, add alias to 2 files, rewrite each call site, rebuild).
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Project name equals the WinRT type name (KeyCredentialManager) so unqualified static calls collide with the app namespace; the accompanying WMC9999 was a red-herring cascade of the C# failure.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent correctly identified the clash, added 'using KeyCredentialManagerWinRT = Windows.Security.Credentials.KeyCredentialManager;' to Content.xaml.cs and SignIn.xaml.cs and rewrote each call.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md subsection on project-name/WinRT-type-name collisions (with the alias fix and a note that WMC9999/WMC1509 is a downstream cascade, not a XAML bug), plus a Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 diagnostic that flags CS0234 into the project's own namespace.

env_issues.issue: WinUI 3 screenshot rendered blank in the non-interactive scoring session (swapchain/DesktopChildSiteBridge cannot be composited by PrintWindow/CopyFromScreen).
env_issues.workaround: Scoring used the UIA tree (33 laid-out elements) as authoritative; this is an eval-environment artifact, not a migration defect.
